The sax version of [Patterns by Ear](patterns-by-ear.qmd). The first few patterns of a set are taught with fingering diagrams.
Then the page plays the rest, one at a time, and you play each back on your saxophone. New to the fingerings? See the
[fingering chart](../lessons/saxophone.qmd#fingering-chart).

```{=html}
<div class="ep-panel">
  <div class="ep-dots" id="es-dots2"></div>
```

## How it works {#how}

- **Written notes.** Everything on this page is in *written* pitch, the notes on your part. The page plays them at the
  pitch your saxophone really sounds (alto a major 6th lower, tenor a 9th, bari an octave and a 6th), and the microphone turns what it
  hears back into written notes. So pick your saxophone above.
- **Range.** Each set is moved to the written key you pick and placed between written D4 and C6, where no low pinky keys or palm keys are
  needed, when it fits.
- **Fingerings.** The usual fingering from the [fingering chart](../lessons/saxophone.qmd#fingering-chart). Your teacher may prefer an
  alternate (for example the bis key for B♭).
- **What counts.** The notes in order; rhythm isn't checked. Each new note must hold steady for about a tenth of a second. To play the
  same note twice, stop the sound briefly between them (tongue it). With *Any octave counts* on, the whole pattern may be an octave away.
  Stopping for more than four seconds starts the try again.
- **The microphone** ignores everything while the page is playing. Headphones still help: a loud room can confuse it.
- **No sax handy?** A MIDI keyboard or wind controller, or the computer keys, count as written notes.
